---
title: "M2: Preliminary Analysis of Reported Opioid Toxicity Death Rates"
---

## Questions and audience

For provincial and regional public-health readers, we examine how reported
crude opioid toxicity death rates vary across Canadian jurisdictions and
years, and whether the male-to-female rate ratio varies. This preliminary
analysis follows Group 4's PHAC project proposal, using 2016-2025 data.

## Source and analytic sample

The source is the fixed public aggregate PHAC file at
`data/SubstanceHarmsData.csv`, identified in the group's intake card as
the September 22, 2026 release, accessed October 26, 2026.

One analytic row represents a region-year, not a person or death.
We select Opioids, Deaths, By year, 2016-2025, and Crude rate, retaining
overall rates and the reported male and female sex categories.
Quarterly data, partial 2026 data, other harms, and stimulants are excluded.
Canada is a separate reference series, not an additional province.

```{r}
#| label: prepare-region-year-data
# AI prompt: Read the PHAC CSV as text using repository-relative paths.
# Select annual opioid-death crude rates for 2016-2025 and reshape overall,
# male, and female values into unique region-years. Preserve zeroes and
# suppression labels, calculate ratios only with a positive female denominator,
# and flag partial-year coverage and the specified 2025 reporting changes.
# Verified: Checked source filters, unique keys, numeric values, zeroes, and raw suppression labels.

library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(knitr)
library(ggplot2)

roots <- c(".", "../../..")
repo_root <- roots[file.exists(file.path(roots, "data/SubstanceHarmsData.csv"))][1]

if (is.na(repo_root)) stop("Cannot find data/SubstanceHarmsData.csv.")

out_dir <- file.path(repo_root, "milestones/m2-preliminary-analysis/submission")
dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

source_df <- read_csv(
  file.path(repo_root, "data/SubstanceHarmsData.csv"),
  col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
  na = character()
)

selected <- source_df |>
  filter(
    Substance == "Opioids",
    Source == "Deaths",
    Time_Period == "By year",
    Year_Quarter %in% as.character(2016:2025),
    Unit == "Crude rate",
    (Specific_Measure == "Overall numbers" & Disaggregator == "") |
      (Specific_Measure == "Sex" & Disaggregator %in% c("Male", "Female"))
  ) |>
  transmute(
    Region,
    Year = as.integer(Year_Quarter),
    measure = case_when(
      Specific_Measure == "Overall numbers" ~ "overall",
      Disaggregator == "Male" ~ "male",
      TRUE ~ "female"
    ),
    raw = trimws(Value)
  )

stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(selected[c("Region", "Year", "measure")]))

is_numeric <- grepl("^[0-9]+([.][0-9]+)?$", selected$raw)

selected$rate <- NA_real_
selected$rate[is_numeric] <- as.numeric(selected$raw[is_numeric])

selected$status <- case_when(
  is_numeric ~ "Reported",
  selected$raw == "Suppr." ~ "Suppressed",
  selected$raw == "n/a" ~ "Unavailable",
  TRUE ~ "Unexpected"
)

stopifnot(!any(selected$status == "Unexpected"))

panel <- selected |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = measure,
    values_from = c(raw, rate, status),
    names_glue = "{measure}_{.value}"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    partial_year = Region == "Nunavut" & Year == 2023,
    definition_change =
      Region %in% c("British Columbia", "Quebec", "Canada") & Year == 2025,
    ratio_rate = if_else(
      !is.na(male_rate) & !is.na(female_rate) & female_rate > 0,
      male_rate / female_rate,
      NA_real_
    ),
    ratio_status = case_when(
      male_status == "Suppressed" |
        female_status == "Suppressed" ~ "Suppressed",
      male_status == "Unavailable" |
        female_status == "Unavailable" ~ "Unavailable",
      female_rate == 0 ~ "Zero denominator",
      !is.na(ratio_rate) ~ "Reported",
      TRUE ~ "Unexpected"
    )
  ) |>
  arrange(Region, Year)

stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(panel[c("Region", "Year")]))
stopifnot(nrow(panel) == 140, n_distinct(panel$Region) == 14)

kable(
  data.frame(
    Step = c(
      "Source CSV rows",
      "Selected rate records",
      "Unique region-years"
    ),
    N = c(nrow(source_df), nrow(selected), nrow(panel))
  ),
  caption = "Selection flow: three rate records become one region-year."
)
```

## Missingness before exclusions

Suppression and unavailability are kept distinct. Reported zeroes stay zero;
they are not missing. A ratio requires two reported rates and a positive
female rate. Ratios use rounded published rates and are approximate.

The denominator below is all 140 selected region-years, including records
later excluded from the full-year summary. Missingness is not assumed random.

```{r}
#| label: missingness-and-export
# AI prompt: Before exclusions, summarize availability of overall, male, female,
# and ratio values across all selected region-years. Include numeric and missing
# counts, missing percentages, and separate counts for suppression, unavailable
# values, and zero denominators. Display and export missingness-summary.csv.
# Verified: Compared all availability categories and percentages with separate base-R counts and the exported CSV.

measures <- c("overall", "male", "female", "ratio")

missingness <- bind_rows(lapply(measures, function(m) {
  v <- panel[[paste0(m, "_rate")]]
  s <- panel[[paste0(m, "_status")]]

  data.frame(
    Measure = m,
    Region_year_N = nrow(panel),
    Numeric_N = sum(!is.na(v)),
    Missing_N = sum(is.na(v)),
    Missing_percent = round(100 * mean(is.na(v)), 1),
    Suppressed_N = sum(s == "Suppressed"),
    Unavailable_N = sum(s == "Unavailable"),
    Zero_denominator_N = sum(s == "Zero denominator")
  )
}))

write_csv(missingness, file.path(out_dir, "missingness-summary.csv"))

kable(
  missingness,
  caption = "Availability before summary exclusions; N counts region-years."
)
```

## Summary eligibility and exclusions

Nunavut 2023 is retained in the availability audit but excluded from the
summary because reporting covers only part of that year. To avoid pooling
the 2025 reporting changes with earlier definitions, the overall and
sex-specific summary for BC, Quebec, and Canada uses 2016-2024.

These three 2025 rows remain in the availability audit. Other jurisdictions
retain 2025. This is a conservative summary convention, not a claim that
all remaining years and jurisdictions have identical ascertainment.

```{r}
#| label: summary-eligibility
# AI prompt: Create a summary dataset excluding partial-year Nunavut 2023 and
# the flagged 2025 records for BC, Quebec, and Canada. Retain the original panel
# for the availability audit and display the number excluded for each reason
# alongside the number of remaining region-years.
# Verified: Checked Nunavut 2023 and the three flagged 2025 rows against PHAC notes and the group's M1 plan.

summary_df <- panel |>
  filter(!partial_year, !definition_change)

kable(
  data.frame(
    Step = c(
      "Selected region-years",
      "Partial-year exclusion",
      "2025 comparability exclusions",
      "Summary-eligible region-years"
    ),
    N = c(
      nrow(panel),
      sum(panel$partial_year),
      sum(panel$definition_change),
      nrow(summary_df)
    )
  ),
  caption = "Excluded rows are retained in the underlying panel and availability audit."
)
```

## Table 1: descriptive summary of available annual rates

This aggregate-data Table 1 reports eligible years, available numeric years,
missing years, and mean (sample SD) by region and measure. It describes
variation across available years, not individual people.

Rates are per 100,000 population; the ratio is unitless. Mean annual rates
are arithmetic summaries, not pooled-period mortality rates. Canada uses
its own PHAC series; it is never calculated by averaging provincial rates.
Different availability and summary windows limit comparisons between rows.

```{r}
#| label: table1-and-export
# AI prompt: Summarize each region and measure using eligible-year N, numeric N,
# missing N, and mean (sample SD) across available annual values. Handle groups
# with zero or one numeric value explicitly, round summaries to two decimals,
# and display and export the same table as table1.csv.
# Verified: Checked numeric-year N, means, and sample SDs with independent base-R summaries and CSV read-back.

mean_sd <- function(x) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]

  if (!length(x)) return("Not available")

  if (length(x) == 1) {
    return(sprintf("%.2f (SD unavailable)", x))
  }

  sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", mean(x), sd(x))
}

table1 <- summary_df |>
  select(Region, Year, all_of(paste0(measures, "_rate"))) |>
  pivot_longer(
    ends_with("_rate"),
    names_to = "Measure",
    values_to = "Rate"
  ) |>
  mutate(Measure = sub("_rate$", "", Measure)) |>
  group_by(Region, Measure) |>
  summarise(
    Eligible_year_N = n(),
    Numeric_N = sum(!is.na(Rate)),
    Missing_N = sum(is.na(Rate)),
    Mean_SD = mean_sd(Rate),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

write_csv(table1, file.path(out_dir, "table1.csv"))

kable(
  table1,
  caption = "Table 1. Available annual-rate summaries; N counts years, not deaths."
)
```

## Preliminary evidence on change

The table below compares 2016 with 2024, before the flagged 2025 changes.
Source labels remain visible instead of being replaced by zero.

```{r}
#| label: endpoint-comparison
# AI prompt: Create a side-by-side table of each region's published overall
# crude rate in 2016 and 2024. Preserve the original suppression and unavailable
# labels, and explain that these endpoints do not describe the full trajectory.
# Verified: Compared the displayed cells directly with the source CSV, including suppressed and unavailable labels.

endpoints <- panel |>
  filter(Year %in% c(2016, 2024)) |>
  select(Region, Year, overall_raw) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Year,
    values_from = overall_raw,
    names_prefix = "Rate_"
  )

kable(
  endpoints,
  caption = "Published overall crude rates per 100,000; two endpoints do not show the full trajectory."
)
```

In PHAC's Canada series, the reported overall rate is 7.8 in 2016 and 16.2
in 2024. This does not imply a steady increase in every intervening year.
For the secondary question, Table 1 summarizes defined annual male-to-female
ratios; unavailable ratios do not imply equal rates.

## Figure 1: annual reported crude death rates

Each panel shows a province or territory in blue and PHAC's Canada rate in
grey. Nunavut 2023 is omitted from the full-year plot. Triangles identify
the 2025 reporting cautions for BC, Quebec, and Canada; their 2025 points
are disconnected from earlier lines. Other 2025 observations remain in the
plot. The panels use the same zero-based vertical scale.

```{r}
#| label: figure-overall-rates
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 11
#| fig-cap: "Annual published crude death rates per 100,000. Blue: jurisdiction; grey: PHAC Canada reference. Gaps preserve suppressed, unavailable, or partial-year data. Triangles mark 2025 reporting cautions; recent data may be revised."
# AI prompt: Follow our M1 plan with one panel per province or territory,
# blue annual crude-rate trends, and a grey PHAC Canada reference. Preserve gaps,
# omit partial-year Nunavut 2023, and show flagged 2025 values as disconnected
# triangles. Use common zero-based axes and explain colours and markers.
# Verified: Checked plotted values against source rates and confirmed partial-year omissions and disconnected caution points.

plot_panel <- panel |>
  mutate(
    plot_rate = if_else(partial_year, NA_real_, overall_rate),
    line_rate = if_else(definition_change, NA_real_, plot_rate),
    plot_ratio = if_else(partial_year, NA_real_, ratio_rate),
    line_ratio = if_else(definition_change, NA_real_, plot_ratio)
  )

jurisdictions <- plot_panel |>
  filter(Region != "Canada")

canada_reference <- plot_panel |>
  filter(Region == "Canada") |>
  select(-Region)

ggplot(jurisdictions, aes(x = Year)) +
  geom_line(
    data = canada_reference,
    aes(y = line_rate),
    colour = "grey65",
    linewidth = 0.5,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = canada_reference,
    aes(y = plot_rate, shape = definition_change),
    colour = "grey65",
    size = 1,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  geom_line(
    aes(y = line_rate),
    colour = "#0072B2",
    linewidth = 0.6,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(y = plot_rate, shape = definition_change),
    colour = "#0072B2",
    size = 1.6,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~Region, ncol = 3) +
  scale_shape_manual(
    values = c("FALSE" = 16, "TRUE" = 17),
    labels = c("Other years", "2025 reporting caution")
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(2016, 2019, 2022, 2025)) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, NA),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.07))
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = "Reported crude deaths per 100,000",
    shape = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    strip.text = element_text(size = 9)
  )
```

## Figure 2: male-to-female rate ratios

A ratio above 1 means the reported male rate is higher than the female
rate. Ratios are undefined when either rate is suppressed or unavailable,
or the female rate is zero. Prince Edward Island and Nunavut have no
defined ratios in this release. Flagged 2025 points are separated here
as a conservative reporting caution, too.

```{r}
#| label: figure-sex-ratios
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 11
#| fig-cap: "Male-to-female crude-rate ratios calculated from rounded published rates. The dashed line marks equal reported rates. Gaps and absent ratios do not imply equality. Reported sex categories are not gender identity."
# AI prompt: Plot annual male-to-female rate ratios by province or territory
# using common zero-based axes and a dashed reference at 1. Preserve gaps and
# disconnected flagged 2025 points, label panels with no defined ratios, and
# explain that missing ratios do not imply equality or describe gender identity.
# Verified: Checked ratios against male and female rates, positive denominators, missing-data gaps, and empty-panel labels.

no_ratio <- jurisdictions |>
  group_by(Region) |>
  summarise(
    no_values = all(is.na(plot_ratio)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(no_values)

ggplot(jurisdictions, aes(x = Year)) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 1,
    linetype = "dashed",
    colour = "grey55"
  ) +
  geom_line(
    aes(y = line_ratio),
    colour = "#0072B2",
    linewidth = 0.6,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(y = plot_ratio, shape = definition_change),
    colour = "#0072B2",
    size = 1.6,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = no_ratio,
    aes(x = 2020.5, y = 0.5),
    label = "No defined ratio",
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 3
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~Region, ncol = 3) +
  scale_shape_manual(
    values = c("FALSE" = 16, "TRUE" = 17),
    labels = c("Other years", "2025 reporting caution")
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(2016, 2019, 2022, 2025)) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, NA),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.07))
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = "Male-to-female rate ratio",
    shape = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    strip.text = element_text(size = 9)
  )
```

## Methods, limitations, and stewardship

The analysis is descriptive and non-causal. We use PHAC's published crude
rates without age standardization, imputation, or hypothesis testing.
Age structure, small populations, varying reporting coverage, preliminary
investigations, and definition changes affect comparability.

Reported sex categories should not be equated with gender identity.
We preserve suppression and do not reconstruct suppressed counts or
identify people. These results can support further descriptive
investigation, but do not identify causes or establish which policy
response would be effective.

Source: [PHAC surveillance release](https://health-infobase.canada.ca/substance-related-harms/opioids-stimulants/).

Coverage and reporting cautions: [PHAC technical notes](https://health-infobase.canada.ca/substance-related-harms/opioids-stimulants/technical-notes.html).
